facts.heading: Anxiety started in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time, and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work change after deputy left
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. Her deputy head left, and she was asked to step up.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of not being capable
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifests in chest tightness
facts.content: When the thought arrives, Hannah's chest goes tight, and she rehearses things in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say in staff meetings.
facts.evidence: I rehearse every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Fear of being replaced
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she was given the job to someone who cannot read.
facts.evidence: That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: No external confirmation of doubt
facts.content: No one has said anything that suggests the fears are valid.
facts.evidence: Has anyone said anything that suggests that? No, that's the strange thing. Nobody has.

facts.heading: Rewriting email to governors
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of appearing stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves' treatment of Hannah
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind.

facts.heading: Feeling of dishonesty to Mr. Hargraves
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: I feel like I'm lying to him. About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what her mother might have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's past career
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's positive reputation
facts.content: People in the village still praise Hannah's mother as a wonderful head.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement and legacy
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago, and a library is named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Mother's comments impact Hannah
facts.content: Hearing her mother's comments makes Hannah feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning. She falls asleep fine.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day. This started in the second week of term.
facts.evidence: since about the second week of term i drink a lot of coffee to get through today which i know

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Exhaustion from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted at the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Ben told Hannah she should just enjoy the situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Lost social connections
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school to talk to anymore.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really.

facts.heading: Line manager role change
facts.content: Hannah is now the line manager and finds it awkward.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Misses school friends
facts.content: Hannah misses her school friends and her class.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Misses children's experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily experience of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Fear about going back
facts.content: Hannah felt fear and a fear of never going back when she cried.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays, we went walking in the lakes

facts.heading: No thoughts about school
facts.content: Hannah did not think about school for ten days during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: And I didn't think about school once for ten days

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: Hannah was a wreck the week before term started.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Couldn't eat on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on Sunday before term started.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This lasted for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A trail of laughing. A good email. It held for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fraud goal
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves walking into meetings without rehearsing and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for evening relaxation
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling after stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and lighter and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: A lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: Sharing bad news with Ben
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are, not even Ben. She finds telling him scary.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about before I am. Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: When to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah is considering telling Ben this week. She might choose a quiet moment on Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: I might try this week. if I choose a quiet moment not on a Sunday evening then I'm Saturday morning perhaps over breakfast he is always in a good mood then

facts.heading: Revisiting evening notebook
facts.content: Hannah is considering trying the evening notebook again for a week, even just one line.
facts.evidence: would you try the evening notebook again just for a week even one line I could I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget
